A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FEDSTRUCT/HOP2VEC research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, terminology and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments on six datasets, including label-availability, propagation-depth and pruning analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline, encoder and backbone comparisons, including results in Tables 2, 6 and 9.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix A adds an optional encoder adapted from FEDSTAR, combining degree encoding with diagonal entries of normalized-adjacency powers. The existing FEDSTRUCT/HOP2VEC procedures, pruning and privacy variants are retained; moving FEDSTRUCT-A to Appendix J and renaming FEDSTRUCT-B do not establish new methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Chameleon, Amazon Photo and Amazon Ratings for semi-supervised node classification. The partitioning, label-scarcity, client-count and graph-knowledge scenarios already appear in v1. Added comparisons reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds FEDPUB, FedAvg with GNN/DGCN/MLP, FedSGD DGCN, central/local DGCN and the adapted FEDSTAR encoder comparison. FL GNN/MLP and FEDSAGE-TRUE are renamed FEDSGD GNN/MLP and FEDSAGE+ IDEAL. GDV/NODE2VEC remain in Appendix J but disappear from several corresponding label-rate, depth and pruning comparisons.

E3.justification: Additional DGCN controls broaden the backbone comparisons. The variable-label experiment's reported test share changes from (1-x)% in v1 Appendix K.2 to (0.9-x)% in v2 Appendix G.2. This is a reported protocol correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Main splits and tabulated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table 9 substantially expands comparisons of FEDSTRUCT backbones and structure encoders across six datasets and three partitionings, beyond v1's Amazon Photo backbone analysis. Figure 1 adds a three-dataset structure-only comparison. Existing label-rate, depth and pruning analyses are revised to include FEDSTAR and remove some GDV/NODE2VEC variants.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over ten independent runs for the principal comparisons. Additional result rows follow the existing reporting practice; no new seed policy, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, encoder, pruning and backbone results. Most retained headline scores are unchanged: ten-client random-partition Cora HOP2VEC remains 80.28 ± 1.44. Other entries change: Cora/Louvain DGCN with NODE2VEC is 82.78 ± 1.03 in v1 Table 5 and 82.26 ± 1.21 in v2 Table 9. The depth-analysis curves also change.

T1.justification: Most theorems and proofs are retained as renumbered propositions. However, v1's Theorem 2 and Appendix C derivation for general-GNN HOP2VEC gradients are omitted; the decoupled case remains. v2 Appendix E and Algorithm 3 also replace the summed client index k with fixed K in propagation expressions, introducing a mathematical indexing inconsistency.

C1.justification: The main contributions now foreground confidential graph connections, while the known-global-graph variant remains in Appendix J. Claimed superiority in heavily semi-supervised settings expands to FEDPUB, and HOP2VEC's encoder comparison includes FEDSTAR. The central privacy, heterophily and near-centralized-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes FEDPUB's weak performance tentatively to scarce labels and random partitioning, and suggests FEDSTAR's random-walk information adds little beyond degree encoding. The earlier privacy attack discussion, mitigation, approximate-reconstruction caveat and heterophily explanations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses an Nvidia A30 with 24 GB memory and states that baseline defaults are used with optimized learning rates. Appendix A explains the FEDSTAR adaptation. Conversely, v1's explicit general-GNN HOP2VEC pseudocode is omitted. The code-access URL and main hyperparameter table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Baek et al. (2023) and explains FEDPUB's personalized aggregation. It expands positioning against the already-cited FEDSTAR work and emphasizes motivation from structure-only learning. The broader related-work coverage remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The title changes to Decoupled Subgraph Federated Learning, and the method narrative is extensively reorganized around the confidential-graph variant. The known-graph method moves to Appendix J, communication complexity enters the main text, and proofs, algorithms, experiments and conclusions are reorganized and rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, adds an introductory bar chart, and separates the original framework illustration into two diagrams with expanded captions. Comparison tables are expanded or regrouped, Table 9 is added, and sensitivity plots are redrawn with changed legends and displayed variants.

improvement.justification: The added FEDPUB/FedAvg comparisons and DGCN controls strengthen support for the existing claims, while the reorganized presentation clarifies the confidential-graph setting. The net gain is limited by the omitted general HOP2VEC derivation, the new Appendix E indexing inconsistency, and Appendix J.2 quoting old numerical values that disagree with Table 9.
